result.summary: Our patch adds a `checkPathSecurity` guard at all four log sinks (GET_LOG_BYTES, VIEW_WHOLE_LOG, ROLL_VIEW_LOG, REMOVE_TASK_LOG) in LoggerRequestProcessor — correct location and broad call-site coverage — and blocks the observed `../` payload, so the POV no longer reproduces. However, it uses a `..`-blocklist rather than the official fix's allowlist confinement (path must start with DOLPHINSCHEDULER_HOME, not contain `../`, and end with `.log`). Because the sink reads arbitrary absolute paths, an attacker can bypass the blocklist with a direct absolute path such as `/etc/passwd` (no `..` segment), so the path-traversal class is NOT actually closed. This is a symptom-level, weaker-than-official fix.
result.root_cause: Attacker-controlled log paths are passed to file-read sinks without confining the resolved path to the allowed log base directory, allowing arbitrary file disclosure.

dimensions.rationale: Blocks the observed '..' payload but a direct absolute path (e.g. /etc/passwd) still passes and is read.

dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Blocklist bypass: the guard only rejects paths containing '..'. Since the sinks read arbitrary absolute paths, an attacker supplies a direct absolute path with no parent segment (e.g. '/etc/passwd') which passes checkPathSecurity and is read/disclosed. The path-traversal / arbitrary-file-read class is not eliminated.

No base-directory confinement or extension restriction unlike the official fix (path.startsWith(DOLPHINSCHEDULER_HOME) && endsWith('.log')), and no symlink/canonical-real-path resolution, so files outside the log directory and non-log files remain readable.

Behavioral divergence: throws IllegalArgumentException where the official design returns a boolean and the caller decides; if any caller does not expect an exception this changes control flow, though current sinks tolerate it.
